cases.name: album_artist
cases.reason: Projects album and artist columns; both join keys are reads.
cases.sql: SELECT a.AlbumId AS album_id, a.Title AS album_title, r.Name AS artist_name FROM Album a JOIN Artist r ON r.ArtistId = a.ArtistId

cases.name: country_revenue
cases.reason: Grouping and HAVING do not turn join keys into output value sources.
cases.sql: SELECT c.Country AS country, SUM(i.Total) AS revenue, COUNT(i.InvoiceId) AS invoice_count FROM Customer c LEFT JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.Country HAVING SUM(i.Total) > 0

cases.name: correlated_latest
cases.reason: The correlation key is read while the scalar aggregate receives invoice dates.
cases.sql: SELECT c.CustomerId AS customer_id, (SELECT MAX(i.InvoiceDate) FROM Invoice i WHERE i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId) AS last_invoice FROM Customer c

cases.name: cte_window
cases.reason: Window value sources include partition and ordering keys under the project lineage policy.
cases.sql: WITH priced AS (SELECT TrackId, GenreId, UnitPrice FROM Track WHERE Milliseconds > 60000) SELECT TrackId AS track_id, SUM(UnitPrice) OVER (PARTITION BY GenreId ORDER BY TrackId ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_price FROM priced

cases.name: case_label
cases.reason: CASE conditions contribute to the CASE result; the separate email filter remains a read only.
cases.sql: SELECT CustomerId AS customer_id, COALESCE(Company, FirstName) AS display_name, CASE WHEN Country = 'USA' THEN City ELSE Country END AS market FROM Customer WHERE Email IS NOT NULL

cases.name: union_contacts
cases.reason: Both branches can supply output values.
cases.sql: SELECT CustomerId AS contact_id, FirstName AS display_name FROM Customer UNION ALL SELECT EmployeeId, FirstName FROM Employee

cases.name: intersect_countries
cases.reason: Both branches are value sources under the documented INTERSECT policy.
cases.sql: SELECT Country AS country FROM Customer INTERSECT SELECT BillingCountry FROM Invoice

cases.name: except_countries
cases.reason: The right side filters membership but supplies no output value under the documented EXCEPT/MINUS policy.
cases.sql: SELECT Country AS country FROM Customer EXCEPT SELECT BillingCountry FROM Invoice

cases.name: derived_projection
cases.reason: Derived aliases retain physical source columns; the price predicate is read only.
cases.sql: SELECT p.TrackId AS track_id, p.Name AS track_name FROM (SELECT TrackId, Name, UnitPrice FROM Track) p WHERE p.UnitPrice >= 1

cases.name: exists_invoice
cases.reason: EXISTS reads invoice keys and totals without adding them to projected customer values.
cases.sql: SELECT c.CustomerId AS customer_id, c.LastName AS last_name FROM Customer c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Invoice i WHERE i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId AND i.Total > 10)

cases.name: quoted_projection
cases.reason: Quoted identifiers and aliases retain exact output names; predicate-only columns remain reads.

cases.name: ranked_tracks
cases.reason: Ranking depends on partition and ordering keys even though it has no value argument.
cases.sql: SELECT TrackId AS track_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY GenreId ORDER BY UnitPrice DESC, TrackId) AS price_rank FROM Track

cases.name: rename_genre
cases.reason: Changes one genre using input parameters; the write target is not separately counted as a relation read.
cases.sql: CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.acc_rename_genre @genre_id INT, @genre_name NVARCHAR(120) AS BEGIN SET NOCOUNT ON; UPDATE Genre SET Name = @genre_name WHERE GenreId = @genre_id; END

cases.name: copy_genres
cases.reason: INSERT SELECT reads the public table and writes the audit fixture.
cases.sql: CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.acc_copy_genres AS BEGIN SET NOCOUNT ON; INSERT INTO ACC_GENRE_AUDIT (GenreId, GenreName) SELECT GenreId, Name FROM Genre WHERE GenreId >= 9000; END

cases.name: genre_count
cases.reason: The function counts public genre rows; it has no writes or user-routine calls.
cases.sql: CREATE FUNCTION dbo.acc_genre_count() RETURNS INT AS BEGIN RETURN (SELECT COUNT(GenreId) FROM Genre); END

cases.name: call_count
cases.reason: Direct facts contain the function call and log write, not the function's transitive Genre read.
cases.sql: CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.acc_call_count AS BEGIN SET NOCOUNT ON; DECLARE @n INT; SET @n = dbo.acc_genre_count(); INSERT INTO ACC_GENRE_COUNT_LOG (ObservedCount) VALUES (@n); END

cases.name: genre_insert
cases.reason: inserted is a transition relation, not a physical catalog object; the trigger writes the audit table.
cases.sql: CREATE TRIGGER dbo.acc_genre_insert ON dbo.Genre AFTER INSERT AS BEGIN SET NOCOUNT ON; INSERT INTO ACC_GENRE_AUDIT (GenreId, GenreName) SELECT GenreId, Name FROM inserted; END

cases.name: genre_update
cases.reason: inserted/deleted are transition relations; the audit receives old and new row values.
cases.sql: CREATE TRIGGER dbo.acc_genre_update ON dbo.Genre AFTER UPDATE AS BEGIN SET NOCOUNT ON; INSERT INTO ACC_GENRE_CHANGES (GenreId, OldName, NewName) SELECT n.GenreId, o.Name, n.Name FROM inserted n JOIN deleted o ON o.GenreId = n.GenreId; END

reference_policy: Manually reviewed direct reads/value-lineage for views; direct object reads/writes/calls and firing owner for routines/triggers. Routine column reads and row-value lineage are outside the scored scope. Transition tables and local variables are not physical catalog objects.
